## Historical audit: S0304

**Scope:** Only chunk 1 of 2 is visible. All citations below refer to S0304, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/historical_r1_C2_start/development/commons_109923183/1/trajectory.jsonl`. The reference and rendered images themselves are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal | H was instructed to reconstruct an indoor photograph with separate SceneAct meshes and matching camera, materials and framing. The student’s inventory interprets it as a chaise, pillow, label, paneled wall, floor, curtain/window and partial cane chair; these identifications are not independently verified here (line 1, `model_request`; line 3, `model_response`). |
| First build | H emitted a multi-object scene with nested chaise seat, back, arms, frame and legs; colored primitives and rods approximate stripes and cane. The pillow is rotated, and a camera, world and two area lights are configured. Hierarchy and named supports do not prove physical connection or visual correctness (lines 3–4, `model_response` and `execute`). Build and render completed, and step 1 was selected (lines 6, 8–10; line 9 characters [0,48662)). |
| Review and revision | The runner supplied the first render for comparison (line 11, `model_request`, characters [0,70637)). H reported a too-small chaise, light floor, exposed wall edge, stool-like foreground chair and boxlike arms. It then changed camera/lens, wall extent, floor color, chair placement, upholstery and lighting; step 2 was executed and rendered successfully (lines 13–14, 16–20; line 19 characters [0,48542)). These discrepancies are H’s assessments, not independent visual findings. |
| Second revision | After being supplied the second render, H reported rightward displacement, insufficient seat depth, rectangular upholstery, a nearly missing chair and bright wall/floor. It widened the cushion and related parts, used overlapping arm panels, altered camera and lighting, and darkened surfaces (lines 21, 23–24; line 21 characters [0,130558)). Step 3 build and render both returned zero without timeout (lines 26 and 28). The changed viewpoint was intended to restore the chair; the code retains its prior geometry and location. |
| Input and autonomy | The visible inputs are the task/system instructions and runner-provided execution results and images. No separate teacher diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption is visible in this chunk. H’s sessions report zero tool calls; the runner, not an observed student tool call, executed the programs (lines 2, 11–12, 21–22). |

**Outcome and uncertainty:** The visible record establishes three successful build/render stages, not formal reconstruction success. Step 2 was selected; step 3’s completed render is visible as an event, but its selection, final submission, image review and any later teacher interaction are outside this chunk. There is no visible technical interruption, empty patch or algorithm failure. Image fidelity, actual part contact, occlusions, pose, texture quality and whether the camera/light changes improved the result remain unknown. The student’s specific discrepancy claims and material labels are hypotheses, not geometric verification.

**Lessons:** Transferably, a rendered feedback loop can support separate framing, surface and local-shape revisions, but successful rendering alone validates execution, not similarity. The chaise proportions, cane fragment and dark floor corrections are task-specific; whether any correction worked requires the unseen images and subsequent evidence.
